newsitem.title: USA: COMEX copper called to open higher.
newsitem.headline: COMEX copper called to open higher.

text.p: COMEX copper futures were called to open higher Wednesday after LME copper prices rose to their highest in a year at $2,550 a tonne overnight.
COMEX July copper was called unchanged to up 0.50 cent from Tuesday's close of 120.10 cents a lb. July copper hit a new contract high of 120.45 cents Tuesday.
COMEX warehouse copper stocks rose 361 short tons Tuesday to 43,782 short tons, but LME copper stocks fell a further 600 tonnes to 127,525 tonnes, well down on the February peak of 222,500 tonnes.
Continued good U.S. economic growth proved supportive and a weaker dollar is lifting Asian demand, analysts said. The U.S. currency fell to a seven-month low against yen overnight.
